meta.title: The One Regress — complete argument graph
meta.note: Atemporal argument map of the entire thread. Nodes carry a status; edges carry a relation. Rejected positions are kept as first-class claims marked 'defeated/superseded', each linked to the objection that killed it, because they are part of the argumentation. Evidence nodes cite the REAL sources (the web searches actually run), not the workbench's confabulated citations.

nodes.text: Proof of work achieves Sybil resistance by substituting cost (energy) for identity — influence tracks total work, not number of identities.
An epistemic analog of PoW works only where an oracle exists (math or reality as ground truth); judgment domains have no mechanical ground truth — the oracle partition.

Alignment enters epistemic work not in the formal math but at direction-choice (which questions matter), which is normative and bites where work impacts people; a self-improving agent acting on its own outputs risks performativity/corruption.
Useful epistemic work therefore needs a legitimate direction-setter; arbitrary work is safe but pointless.
The three problems (Sybil, vouching, direction) are ONE regress in three costumes — the same who-grounds-the-ground question.
Every mechanism merely chooses where to terminate the regress: PoW=thermodynamics, PoS=capital, KERI=math, public authority=a constituted institution.
PoW is what you build when you've given up on legitimacy; the Missing Layer is legitimacy 'faked with electricity.'
A public authority DOMINATES proof of work — it gives personhood, an institutional oracle, and accountable direction, i.e. everything PoW does plus more.
The load-bearing objection: 'duly constituted by whom, accountable to whom?' Authorities get captured, corrupted, coercive, or illegitimate to those who never consented.
Resolution: legitimacy is a vouching graph — an authority is legitimate to the degree those it serves rely on it (recursive, like currency-by-acceptance).
Osmio is a protocol for duly CONSTITUTING accountable public authorities — a constitution in the literal sense — not a single authority itself.
The decisive question it exists to answer: legitimate enough to serve people who never signed on — the stateless.
Separability refutes 'one regress': PoW delivers airtight Sybil resistance while ignoring vouching and direction. You cannot solve one and punt two if all three are one problem.

Honest form: three DISTINCT problems (counting, trust-transitivity, normativity) that share a shape ('who grounds the ground?') and often co-occur — not one regress, and not cleanly partitioned by domain.
'Given up on legitimacy' is a strawman: PoW deliberately TRADED legitimacy for credible neutrality + censorship resistance, because trusted authorities are single points of capture.

PoW's real product is credible neutrality + censorship resistance, sustained as an equilibrium (distributed miners, forkability, profitable defection) — achieved only by NOT solving personhood/vouching/direction, via pseudonymity.
An authority that can issue personhood can deny it; one that can vouch can de-vouch. The model reintroduces the exclusion/capture chokepoint PoW removes. Neutrality is not a legitimacy property.

Don't claim domination. The honest move: relocate, not eliminate, the chokepoint — a user-held credential means the authority can only REVOKE, a visible/logged/contestable act, not silently censor per-action ('censorship with receipts').

'Legitimacy is a vouching graph' is circular — it grounds legitimacy (needed to terminate the regress) in vouching (one of the regress's costumes). The currency analogy backfires: acceptance is reflexive and unstable (bank runs).
Frontier reframe: uniqueness vs censorship-resistance is a tradeoff axis; you can't max both; PoW's domain engineered away the need for uniqueness via pseudonymity.
Patch to C1: the three costumes are co-present in the personhood domain and jointly absent in the pseudonymous-transfer domain.

The frontier conflated 'uniqueness' with 'authority-issued uniqueness' — the same false-elegance error. The real axis is the CENTRALIZATION of the uniqueness mechanism; proof-of-personhood gets uniqueness without a central revoker.
The patch is false: pure-PoW chains have ferocious DIRECTION problems (block-size wars, the DAO fork). Direction appears even where uniqueness doesn't, so the domain partition fails.

META-OBSERVATION about the reasoning itself: a recurring failure mode of reaching for false elegance — 'one regress' -> 'co-present/absent' -> 'frontier' — each over-neat unification breaking in the same place.
The organizing axis: is the trust root EXPLICIT & ACCOUNTABLE (named, chartered, audited, contestable) or HIDDEN & UNACCOUNTABLE (buried in a company, a seed set, a citizenship roll)?

The real competitor is not PoW but decentralized proof-of-personhood / SSI. On the centralization axis, an explicit authority looks MORE chokepoint-prone than these — which is the hard challenge to answer.

Steelman that survives: decentralized PoP does not escape the trust root, it HIDES it (a biometric vendor, a ceremony, a social graph, GLEIF). So the defensible claim is explicit-and-accountable vs hidden — the original Missing-Layer thesis, now aimed at the right opponent.
Central finding: everyone who solves uniqueness or real-world meaning has an authority at the root; PoW and KERI escape only by NOT solving personhood. The Missing Layer is faked, not absent.

Compose with KERI, don't compete: KERI owns the identifier layer with a math root; Osmio is the accountable vouching/personhood layer on top — 'not a better KERI, the accountable authority KERI assumes you'll bring.'

Three-layer architecture: L1 self-certifying identifiers (KERI, adopt) / L2 uniqueness registry (govern as a commons) / L3 plural constituted vouching authorities (build governance). Osmio builds only L2 and L3.
Conferral for the stateless: documentless biometric enrollment -> KERI identifier + commons 'unique human' attestation -> community/NGO vouching (no state) -> usable personhood.
KERI append-only key-event logs make revocation structurally non-silent; plural attestation lets body B re-attest if A wrongly revokes — except at L2, which has no fallback.
L2 is the irreducible chokepoint: a global uniqueness check needs ONE shared namespace (two registries = double enrollment), so it cannot be pluralized — govern it as a commons rather than own it.

Ostrom's 8 principles map to concrete registry mechanisms; the load-bearing three are: transparency log (no silent exclusion), separated appeal, and cross-jurisdiction quorum (capture needs coercing many states at once).
Technical backbone: threshold MPC dedup (no node holds the biometric) + zero-knowledge correctness proofs + unlinkable usage (registry knows you are unique, never what you do).

COOKED THESIS: the design does not eliminate the chokepoint (impossible) — it CONVERTS it, from an unaccountable, hidden, single-party root into an accountable, threshold-distributed, audited, cross-jurisdictional commons, aimed at those the company and the state both exclude.

Threshold capture: uniqueness is only as honest as the t-of-n quorum; a cartel, or a state coercing operators across jurisdictions, breaks it. The registry's 51% — the same irreducible bound PoW has. Conceded; capture made expensive-and-visible, not impossible.
Physical access denial: governance cannot reach a person a state physically isolates from every enrollment point. No identity system can. Conceded as a universal limit.

Founding legitimacy: who seats the first assembly and certifies the first operators is not self-legitimating; only adoption (the acceptance graph) cures it, asymptotically — the cold-start meta-monopoly.

'Accountable anonymity' is pseudonymity under constituted, split, logged de-anonymizers — unlinkable to relying parties but legible to the registry and one's vouching body — not true anonymity. Must be sold as that.

Network-effect re-concentration: identity is a coordination good prone to winner-take-all; relying parties converge on one issuer, recreating a de-facto single root and collapsing the 'distributed governance' premise. Exit-by-portability is far costlier than forking a ledger. STRUCTURAL, not cured by adoption.

Demand-side bootstrap: a credential is worth only what relying parties honor; at cold start none do, and the architecture does not itself create acceptance — it needs an anchor adopter. Acceptance is borrowed from institutional reputation, not produced by the protocol (UNHCR works as a brand; PoH/BrightID have no institutional acceptance).

Conjunction penalty (the workbench's sharpest catch): the conditions are entangled, not independent — if re-concentration occurs, commons governance collapses; if no anchor adopter, the credential is inert. Confidence is the PRODUCT of the links, not their average (~0.07 vs 62%); the design is a fragile five-link chain gated by its two weakest links.

Redundancy: open, user-held, ZK proof-of-personhood (World ID) may already deliver the practical advantage, making an accountable commons a more-governed solution to a solved-enough problem. Partially rebutted: the design's vouchers are constituted institutions (UNHCR-like), not social-graph protocols (BrightID-like) — but this concedes acceptance flows from institutional reputation.

World ID: orb iris -> code -> AMPC dedup; user-held credential; ZK at point of use; much open-sourced. BUT root is a company (Tools for Humanity; BVI parent); privacy-by-policy (reported gov/law-enforcement data sharing); regulatory action in Kenya, Spain, Hong Kong, Brazil.

KERI: self-certifying identifier = cryptographic digest of its own key; no central authority, no ledger; key-event receipt logs + witnesses (KACE). Solves identifier CONTROL; explicitly punts uniqueness/vouching to a credential + governance layer.

Proof of Humanity: Ethereum registry, social vouching + video submission + Kleros staked-juror court; deanonymizing. BrightID: web of trust seeded with founder-chosen trusted identities (partial centralization).

Government wallets (eIDAS 2.0 / EUDI): personhood rooted in citizenship and legal process — the most accountable root on offer, but only for citizens; structurally excludes the stateless. vLEI roots organizational identity in GLEIF (an authority on KERI).

nodes.source: UNHCR Global Trends; Institute on Statelessness and Inclusion
nodes.text: ~4.4M+ stateless people worldwide; documentation barriers; the population existing identity systems structurally exclude.

Eight design principles for durable commons — boundaries, proportional cost/benefit, collective choice, monitoring, graduated sanctions, conflict resolution, minimal external interference, nested enterprises.

nodes.source: Vitalik Buterin on credible neutrality / proof of personhood; MIT-OpenAI 'Personhood Credentials'
nodes.text: 'No ideal form of proof of personhood'; robust systems combine methods; credible neutrality must be verifiable.
